evidence.quote:
Factual statements are generally accurate and supported by relevant and
up-to-date citations; however, some higher-level interpretive claims and model-specific
propositions rely primarily on authorial synthesis and would benefit from clearer signaling as
conceptual in nature or from the addition of supporting references where available.

Furthermore, Reviewer #1 (Dr. Carlit Casey) states that the manuscript could benefit from
clearer signaling as conceptual in nature or from additional references where available. This
is because of a couple of ungrounded statements. So, we agree and have implemented two
complementary improvements (a) and (b):
(a) Clearer signaling of epistemic status
Epistemic-status paragraph for the model: We added an explicit statement
clarifying that the relational links within the model are conceptual propositions
○

○

○

○




derived from comparative synthesis, intended as testable hypotheses rather than
empirically established causal claims.
(b) Additional supporting references where feasible
For claims about the integration of disciplinary, didactic, and contextual
knowledge—and the role of situated cognitive skills in practice—we reinforced
citation support with widely recognized international and Spanish scholarship.
We also reviewed several interpretive passages and refined the language to avoid
over-strong generalizations (e.g., replacing categorical formulations with
appropriately modalized phrasing where the claim is interpretive).
These changes maintain the manuscript’s theoretical contribution while aligning the
presentation of claims with standard scholarly expectations: statements are supported with
citations, and conceptual claims are transparently framed as propositions emerging from
synthesis.
○

○

4. About the assessment of the support on citations
Some statements were not supported by citations. We addressed this by (i) strengthening
citation support for selected high-level claims (particularly those concerning integrated
professional profiles and situated cognitive skills), and (ii) explicitly labeling model links as
conceptual propositions where the claim is interpretive. We also revised language in a small
number of passages to avoid any unintended implication of empirically established
causality.
